items.q: How much harder did outreach get in the AI era?
items.a: Engineers contacted per hire went ~**500–700** (5 years ago) → ~**1,500** (2 years ago) → **~5,000 today**. When every candidate gets **1,000 cold emails**, nothing feels special.

items.q: What restores signal when spam is everywhere?
items.a: **Meaning comes from scarcity.** Trust, relationships, and access matter more than another talent-graph search.

items.q: What is Paraform's core product bet?
items.a: **Augment recruiters, don't replace them** — automate ~**70–80%** of grunt work; keep the last ~**20% human touch**. They've paid out **$50M+** to recruiters.

items.q: Why did referral bounties fail but pro recruiters work?
items.a: Casual referrers **don't know enough candidates** and don't return. Independent recruiters/agencies retain because it's their **job**, they're connected, and they're financially motivated.

items.q: How many candidates should matching surface?
items.a: **3–4 high-fit options**, not 1,000 choices — constrained matching beats infinite choice overload.

items.q: What did founders say the #1 problem was?
items.a: Almost all said **hiring** — at about **$40K/hire**. Five hires/year ≈ a salary equivalent of willingness to pay.

items.q: Why isn't "find great engineers" the real bottleneck?
items.a: Finding talent is easy; **getting a response** requires trust/access. A Meta engineer may ignore a stranger but consider a **trusted friend's** outreach.

items.q: How deep should you dig before building?
items.a: Surface "hiring is hard" → root cause: **trust, access, relationships**. Kim: "If you think you're going deep you're **probably still not deep enough**."

items.q: What proof point unlocked Paraform's seed?
items.a: **Hightouch** had a director of engineering role open **18 months**; Paraform filled it in **1.5 months** → investor intro → seed term sheet **same day**, no pitch deck.

items.q: How did a health scare shape Kim's urgency?
items.a: At 18 a lung scare reframed life into **3-year terms**, not 65-year deferral — **finite-horizon urgency** that stuck even after the false alarm.

items.q: What scale has that conviction produced?
items.a: Raised **$65M**, **10× revenue in 2025**, customers including Palantir, Rippling, Decagon, and Bridge — by staying in the hiring problem through failed pivots.
